name: Logarithmic spiral arms
description: Grand-design spirals show two or more sharply wound arms of blue young stars and pink star-forming knots on a smoother yellow disc.
physics: Density waves and shearing differential rotation organise star formation into trailing arcs with pitch angle of roughly 10-30 degrees.
visualSignature: arms bluer than the inter-arm disc, bulge yellow
arms fray into feathers and spurs

name: Dust lanes along the inner arm edge
description: Dark, ragged lanes trace the inner (concave) edges of spiral arms and silhouette the bulge and disc, especially in edge-on and inclined galaxies.
physics: Dust grains absorb and scatter blue light; the dust is concentrated in the thin cold gas layer where arms compress it. Extinction is wavelength-dependent so lanes redden what shines through.
visualSignature: lanes thin and offset to the inner arm edge
reddened rim where lane is partly transparent
filament and flocculent texture, not smooth bands

description: Spiral arms are studded with compact pink-red knots and blue star-cluster clumps that make arms look beaded rather than smooth.

blue-white cluster cores inside pink halos
